analysis: Examined the added changelog (changelog.d/glm-variable-frame-rate-video.md lines 1-3) and the docs/architecture/inference.md edits (head 3, 810-813, 829). The changes document that GLM-5.3-Flash video processing now accepts variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks, indexing frames in presentation order and timing frame i at i/nominalFrameRate before the unchanged 2 FPS sampler. Base also documented that VFR video was refused with a deterministic 400. These are documentation-only changes. No Swift source in this batch shows the processor implementation (GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset, GLM5NextVisionBudget). The docs state the decoded-frame cap (maximumDecodedBytes, 512 MiB), media reservation, video token ceiling and 28,532 prepared-pixel cap remain in force. Media requests are still excluded from prefix lookup/capture (CBv2Request.permitsHybridCheckpoint), so T-041 exposure is unchanged. Relevant threats are TB-007 decoder attack surface/availability (T-029-style resource use) and T-050 inline-video plaintext handling. Accepting VFR widens accepted inputs: adversarial VFR timestamps (huge sample counts, zero or near-zero durations, a tiny nominalFrameRate) could change the sampled frame count or the frames decoded up to the last sample. Integration must verify in source that: (1) nominalFrameRate of zero, NaN or an extreme value is refused; (2) the number of frames decoded up to the last sampled index stays bounded by the duration/frame caps and the decode budget; (3) the visual-token ceiling is computed before decoding from the same index/timing model. No regression is evidenced in the supplied docs, so no finding is reported.
